model: The Popit is the in-game editing layer for the thing under the cursor. In LittleBigPlanet its menu contains the Popit Cursor, Goodies Bag, Tools Bag, Stickers & Decorations, Player Color and the player's colour pairs; selecting an object and opening its Tweak menu changes that object. This surface applies the same model to a shell window or a live HUD cell: it is not a CREATE/PLAY launcher and it does not own a second desktop. The root stays mounted; opening a section reveals a contextual child beside it and Back closes the child.

elements.acceptance: The surface is a persistent root plus a contextual child anchored beside the selected cell; it never draws CREATE/PLAY cards or a mode tab.
A click outside closes the surface; the dismiss panel is the only full-screen hit-testable child.
The selected cell is outlined in the Player Colour; the halo follows the target's measured rectangle and is never hit-testable.
The root is one persistent instrument with six section rows; it stays mounted while a child opens and only shifts aside.
One hit-testable row per section with its code, name and current hint; the open section carries Active.
The root foot carries one dot per section and marks the open one On.
The child reveals beside the root for one section; opening another section replaces its body only, never the root.
The child head carries Back and the section title; Back closes the child and leaves the root mounted.
Back is a hit-testable control, not a keyboard-only convention; closing keeps the root's section state.
The child title names the open section in uppercase, not a launcher mode.
Every group carries one uppercase labeller and one dashed rule, so the child reads as a list of groups.
The Cursor section lists only targets the shell can bind to a live panel or cell; choosing one retargets the editor.
The Palette section lists all 37 player colours grouped by game and marks the chosen one; picking one is reported to the shell for the saved profile.
The Goodies Bag lists paper, card, glass, tint, ink, accent and bare; picking one emits a material edit for the selected cell.
Stickers & Decorations lists edge, stitch, tag, corners and none; the treatment is tinted by the Player Colour.
The Tools Bag exposes the cell's Tweak values: corners, border width and opacity.
Player Color lists the scheme roles plus Default; the chosen role recolours the cursor halo, decoration and tool accent.
The root header carries the chosen pair's three-colour band and its name, opening the Palette section.
One hit-testable tile per pair with a three-band swatch, the game name and the chosen state.
Classic is the opt-out: it removes the pair class and restores the scheme's own roles without discarding the chosen pair.
One target row per live window/cell with its title, kind and detail; the current target carries Selected.
The root header names the surface, not a launcher mode.
The root names the selected cell and whether it is a cell, a live panel or a window.
One hit-testable material, decoration or colour item with a palette-derived swatch and Hover/Selected states.
Each Tweak value is a separate hit-testable button; the current value carries Selected.
Restore this cell clears every Popit write and returns the native panel to the values captured before the edit.
The footer names the selected cell or the edit that just landed.
An edit writes the material, decoration, colour, radius, border and opacity on the actual bound panel through recorded inline writes.
The recorded writes are restored in reverse order; a dead panel is not touched.
A style travels in the cell's own layout row as a fixed alphabet, never as free-form CSS or a second stylesheet.
The host accepts a fifth comma field only when it matches the same alphabet and rejects an unknown material, colour, decoration or value.

The popit= row grammar is owned by the module: the shell snapshot calls encodeProfile and the load path calls decodeProfile, so the arrangement and the pair slug cannot drift between writer and reader. An unknown pair is dropped rather than painted.
The chosen pair travels as pair:<slug> in the popit row; the host validates the slug and the client drops an unknown one instead of painting a wrong palette.
Reduced motion is a real suppression path set by the host; the same state and order remain and only the transitions stop.
The surface prefers a side that does not cover the target, clamps to the screen and falls back beside or over the target rather than refusing to open.
